- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops below 1.0, model overcorrects downward; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price volatility >2%; forecast should align with 14d moving average.
- If news volume is high (≥2.0) and sentiment is volatile (±0.5+ change), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- When sentiment is flat (±0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
